capabilities.description: List scoped terminal sessions available to the agent.
Return bridge runtime status and policy configuration.
List user-attached files in the current AI chat scope.
Read a user-attached file from the current AI chat scope.
Cancel in-flight operations for a chat session.
Resume write operations for a cancelled chat session.
Get metadata for a single scoped session.

Request reconnect of a disconnected session in the current scope, preserving its tab and workspace. Does not restart connected sessions or replay commands. Returns acknowledgement, not shell readiness. Recovery is limited to three attempts with 2/5 second backoff in a 120 second incident; inspect authentication or exhausted recovery instead of retrying indefinitely.

Inspect and recover a scoped disconnected session in place. Automatically applies bounded reconnect/backoff for up to 20 seconds per call and reports ready only once the transport is restored (still-offline budgets return pending); shellReady is advisory (true/false/null) and, when unconfirmed, nextAction "inspect_shell" asks you to verify the prompt before typing. Stops for authentication, busy jobs, cancellation or unavailable state. Never creates tabs or executes/replays commands.
Close a terminal session previously opened by host_open in the current AI scope.
Execute a short command in a terminal session and wait for completion.
Start a long-running command in a terminal session.
Poll incremental output from a long-running terminal job.
Stop a long-running terminal job.
List a remote directory over the session file backend (SFTP or SCP-mode).
Read a remote file over the session file backend (SFTP or SCP-mode).
Write a remote file over the session file backend (SFTP or SCP-mode).
Download a remote file to a local path.
Upload a local file to a remote path.
Get remote file metadata over the session file backend (SFTP or SCP-mode).
Get the remote home directory for a session.
Create a remote directory over the session file backend (SFTP or SCP-mode).
Delete a remote file or directory over the session file backend (SFTP or SCP-mode).
Rename a remote file or directory over the session file backend (SFTP or SCP-mode).
Change remote file permissions over the session file backend (SFTP or SCP-mode).
Get host metadata from the vault.
List saved hosts in the vault (metadata only — no passwords or keys).

Open a vault host by reusing its existing session when its connection settings still match (connected or connecting, including auto-reconnecting — same sessionId, no duplicate tab). Only opens a new terminal tab when no usable session for this host exists, or when newTab is true. Inactive disconnected and restored tabs are not reused. Returns the sessionId so you can run terminal/SFTP tools against it. Use vault_hosts_list first when you only know the label or hostname.
Create vault hosts from structured host objects. Use when the user wants to add/create a host (Vault → Hosts). NOT for Vault → Notes sidebar documentation.
Update selected fields on an existing vault host. Use vault_hosts_list first to resolve the hostId.
Delete a saved vault host by id. Use vault_hosts_list first to resolve the hostId.

Parse known host export file formats (PuTTY, MobaXterm, CSV, SecureCRT, FinalShell, ssh_config) into vault hosts. For arbitrary unstructured text, map to host objects and use vault_hosts_create instead.
Read host metadata notes attached to a saved host (Host Details panel — not Vault sidebar Notes).
Update host metadata notes on a saved host (Host Details panel — not Vault sidebar Notes).
List notes in Vault → Notes (markdown notes visible in the vault sidebar).

Read or search a Vault → Notes entry by exact id, at most 6000 characters per call. Content is only the returned range, not necessarily the whole note. Follow nextOffset with expectedUpdatedAt until null for a complete read; query searches only return matching excerpts. Read every range without query before summarizing the whole note or replacing its content; never treat unread text as absent. For long notes, retain section summaries rather than repeatedly loading all ranges. If the note changed, restart.
Create a note in Vault → Notes sidebar (markdown documentation). NOT for adding SSH hosts — use vault_hosts_create for that.
Update an existing Vault → Notes entry by id.
Delete a Vault → Notes entry by id.
Import one or more markdown documents into Vault → Notes. Titles come from an explicit title, the first level-one heading, or the file name. NOT for adding SSH hosts.
List reusable vault identities without passwords, private keys, or passphrases.
List reusable proxy profiles without credentials.
List vault groups and their safe default settings.
Create a vault group with optional default connection settings.
Update or rename a vault group and its default connection settings.
Delete a vault group, moving its hosts to the root unless deleteHosts is true.
List code snippets stored in the vault.
Get a single code snippet from the vault.
Run a vault snippet or automation script in a terminal session. Text snippets paste shell commands; scripts (kind=script) run via the nct JavaScript runtime.
Create a vault snippet or automation script (set kind=script for nct automation).
Update an existing vault snippet or automation script by id.
Delete a vault snippet or automation script by id.
List automation scripts (kind=script) in the vault.
Get a single automation script including JavaScript source.
Create an automation script using the nct JavaScript API. Call scripts_reference first when authoring nct automation.
Update an automation script by id (partial fields).
Delete an automation script and remove host connect bindings.
Run an automation script in a terminal session via the nct runtime. Set wait=true to block until completion.
Return Netcatty automation script syntax: nct API, triggers, host targeting, and source wrapping rules.
List automation script runs (optionally filter by sessionId).
Stop a running automation script by runId.
Pause a running automation script by runId.
Resume a paused automation script by runId.
Set host IDs, dynamic group paths, or targetsAllHosts for an automation script. onConnect host IDs sync host connect queues.
List resolved onConnect automation scripts for a host (global, dynamic group, then host queue).
Set ordered onConnect script IDs for a host (host-specific queue; globals run separately).
List persisted port forwarding rules.
List active port forwarding tunnels.
Create a persisted port forwarding rule.
Update a persisted port forwarding rule.
Duplicate a persisted port forwarding rule.
Delete a persisted port forwarding rule.
Start a port forwarding tunnel for a rule.
Stop an active port forwarding tunnel.
Read stored tool output by handle id when a prior tool result was truncated.
Get information about the current workspace, including all terminal sessions and their connection status.
Get detailed information about a specific terminal or SFTP session.
Read a bounded slice of the current terminal screen or scrollback from the active AI scope.
Search the web for current information when configured in AI settings.
Fetch and read the content of an HTTPS URL.

hostId.description: Vault host ID to open. Use vault_hosts_list / host_get to resolve id from label or hostname.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace ID or current (active workspace). Applies to newly opened sessions; reused sessions retain their placement. Omit for a standalone tab.

newTab.description: true or false. Force a brand-new tab even when a session for this host already exists. Default false — reuse the existing session.

hosts.description: JSON array of host objects you extracted from the user's text. Each object: hostname (required; host/ip aliases accepted), label (name alias accepted), port, username, password, keyPath or keypath (local private-key file path), passphrase (saved passphrase for that key path), group, tags (array or comma-separated string), notes (Host Details remarks — NOT Vault sidebar Notes), protocol (ssh|telnet|local), os (linux|windows|macos).

dryRun.description: Set to true to validate and preview without writing to the vault.

skipDuplicates.description: Set to false to create even when a matching host already exists (default true).

username.description: New login username. Clears any reusable identity binding so this value takes effect.

password.description: New password without changing key-based login. Password identities are detached so the new value takes effect. Empty string clears it and blocks inherited saved passwords. Pair with keyPath set to an empty string to switch from key login to password login.

savePassword.description: Set to true or false to enable or disable saved passwords. Pass true when setting a new password after clearing one.

keyPath.description: Local private-key file path. Empty string clears and blocks an inherited path.

passphrase.description: Saved passphrase for the host's local private-key path. Empty string clears the saved passphrase.

group.description: New group path. Empty string moves the host to the root.

tags.description: JSON array or comma-separated tag names. Empty string clears tags.

notes.description: Host Details remarks. Empty string clears notes.

protocol.description: New protocol: ssh, telnet, local, or serial.

os.description: Operating system override: auto (default), linux, windows, macos, freebsd, or unknown. Use auto to use detected system information; network device mode is separate.

identityId.description: Reusable identity ID from vault_identities_list. Empty string detaches the identity.

jumpHostIds.description: JSON array of vault host IDs in jump order. Empty array clears the chain.

proxyProfileId.description: Reusable proxy ID from vault_proxy_profiles_list. Empty string clears it.

startupCommand.description: Command to run after connecting. Empty string clears it.

environmentVariables.description: JSON object or array of {name,value} entries. Empty object clears them.

serialConfig.description: JSON object for serial connections: path, baudRate, and optional dataBits, stopBits, parity, flowControl, localEcho, lineMode, backspaceBehavior (default or ctrl-h), byteOrientedBackspace (boolean, default false; enable only for devices that delete bytes rather than characters). Existing backspaceBehavior and byteOrientedBackspace are preserved when omitted.

format.description: Import format: csv, putty, mobaxterm, securecrt, finalshell, ssh_config, or auto to detect from text.

text.description: Exported host data text to import.

query.description: Optional case-sensitive literal search, 1-200 UTF-16 units. Returns an excerpt starting at the next match at/after offset; matchOffset=null means no match. Keep query when continuing search.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Pass note.updatedAt from the first read on subsequent reads to detect changes; restart if it changed.

modelDescriptionHints.session.environment: Call this first for any task involving a live Netcatty terminal, remote server, SSH session, SFTP path, or terminal tab. Select the target by label or hostname, then pass its sessionId to terminal and SFTP tools. Call it again after the user opens, closes, or renames a session.
modelDescriptionHints.terminal.execute: Use this instead of the local shell when the command is intended for a Netcatty terminal or remote host. Call get_environment first to resolve the sessionId. Use only for commands expected to finish within about 60 seconds. For long-running commands use terminal_start and terminal_poll. Commands run in an isolated subshell of the visible terminal: the user sees the output live, but shell state such as cd, export, or set does not persist between calls — use absolute paths or combine cd with the command (cd /path && cmd).
modelDescriptionHints.terminal.start: Use this instead of the local shell for long-running commands on a Netcatty terminal or remote host. Call get_environment first to resolve the sessionId. Prefer for builds, scans, log-following, or anything likely to exceed about 2 minutes. Shell state such as cd or export does not persist between calls — combine cd with the command.
modelDescriptionHints.terminal.poll: Wait at least about 30 seconds between polls unless output justifies checking sooner.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.host.notes.get: Host metadata notes on a saved host — not Vault → Notes sidebar entries.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.host.notes.set: Host metadata notes on a saved host — not Vault → Notes sidebar entries. Prefer vault_notes_create/update when the user wants vault notes they can open in the Notes sidebar.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.host.open: Reuse-first: if this hostId already has a connected or connecting session with matching connection settings (including one auto-reconnecting after a drop, which keeps the same sessionId), that sessionId is returned and no new tab is opened — retry terminal_execute against it rather than reopening the host. Open a new tab only when get_environment shows no session for the host, when the task truly needs a parallel connection, or with newTab true. Call session_close when finished only for a newly opened session (reused is not true). A reused session keeps its original owner; do not close it as task cleanup. Disconnected or restored tabs needing user action are not reused. Connection may still be establishing when the tool returns — use get_environment or wait briefly before terminal_execute if needed. Auth prompts (passphrase / keyboard-interactive) still require the user in the Netcatty UI.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.host.list: Use when the user names a saved Netcatty host but get_environment has no matching live session. Resolve the hostId here, call host_open, then call get_environment to obtain the new sessionId.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.host.import: Only for text in known export formats (PuTTY reg, MobaXterm ini, CSV template, SecureCRT, FinalShell JSON, ssh_config). If attached host text is unknown or auto-detection fails, use read_attachment content, extract fields yourself, and call vault_hosts_create.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.hosts.create: Use when the user wants to add/create a host in Vault → Hosts (创建主机、SSH 连接凭据). NOT for Vault → Notes sidebar docs. Put SSH password in password, or a local private-key file path in keyPath. If that key is encrypted and the user supplied its passphrase, put it in passphrase so later connections do not prompt. Put long remarks/admin tables in host notes. Never fall back to vault_notes_create if this fails.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.host.update: Update only fields the user requested. Use vault_hosts_list first to resolve hostId. Empty group, tags, notes, password, keyPath, or passphrase values clear those fields or saved credentials.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.host.delete: Permanently deletes one saved host. Use vault_hosts_list first to resolve hostId and rely on the normal write approval flow before deleting.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.note.create: Use ONLY when the user wants markdown documentation in Vault → Notes sidebar (保险箱笔记). Do NOT use when the user asked to create/add a host — use vault_hosts_create instead.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.note.update: Update an existing Vault → Notes entry (visible in the vault notes sidebar).
modelDescriptionHints.vault.note.import: Import generated or attached markdown into Vault → Notes. Use content plus fileName for one document, or documents for a batch. This creates notes; it does not add SSH hosts. Confirm mode asks the user to approve the import.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.snippets.run: Text snippets (kind=snippet) paste shell commands with optional named placeholders written with two curly braces on each side. Scripts (kind=script) run via nct JavaScript runtime — use scripts_run for script-only workflows.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.snippets.create: Create vault snippets (shell text) or scripts (kind=script, nct JavaScript). For multi-step terminal automation use kind=script and call scripts_reference.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.scripts.run: Runs automation scripts in the nct JavaScript sandbox. Use wait=true to block until completion. Prefer over terminal_execute for await nct.screen.* workflows.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.scripts.create: Create nct automation scripts. Call scripts_reference first to learn the nct API, triggers, and source wrapping rules.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.scripts.reference: Returns full Netcatty automation script syntax reference (nct API, triggers, host targeting). Read before authoring scripts.
modelDescriptionHints.vault.host.connectScripts.set: Sets per-host onConnect script queue order. Global and matching dynamic-group scripts run first automatically.
